title: Olfactory Groove Meningioma & Foster Kennedy Syndrome
summary: A comprehensive guide to the neuro-ophthalmic manifestations of Olfactory Groove Meningiomas (OGMs), specifically detailing the classic Foster Kennedy Syndrome (FKS) triad of ipsilateral optic atrophy, contralateral papilledema, and anosmia.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Olfactory groove meningiomas (OGMs) arise from the arachnoid cap cells of the cribriform plate and planum sphenoidale. They represent approximately 10% of all intracranial meningiomas. Because of their slow growth and the spaciousness of the subfrontal area, they often reach massive sizes before detection. Foster Kennedy Syndrome is the classic but rare ophthalmic presentation resulting from these tumors' mass effect and intracranial pressure elevation.

rows: Low mitotic rate; Meningothelial, Fibrous, Psammomatous.
4-19 mitoses/10HPF; Brain invasion; High N:C ratio.

sections.title: The Foster Kennedy Syndrome Triad
content: 1. Ipsilateral Optic Atrophy: Direct compression of the optic nerve by the tumor leads to primary axonal death.
2. Contralateral Papilledema: Raised intracranial pressure (ICP) from the mass causes axonal transport stasis in the unaffected nerve.
3. Anosmia: Destruction or compression of the olfactory bulbs/tracts (earliest clinical sign, often missed).

sections.title: Ocular Examination Findings
content: Visual Acuity: Unilateral or bilateral decline (central scotoma).
Color Vision: Dyschromatopsia out of proportion to VA loss.
Pupils: Ipsilateral Relative Afferent Pupillary Defect (RAPD).
Fundus: Pale disc (Ipsi) vs. Hyperemic/Blurred margins (Contra).
Visual Fields: Central/paracentral scotoma or junctional scotoma.
Motility: Occasional 6th nerve palsy due to raised ICP (False localizing sign).

rows: Isointense to gray matter; marked homogenous enhancement with Gadolinium.
Hyperintense (suggests soft consistency) or Hypointense (suggests calcification).
Hyperostosis of the planum sphenoidale; tumor calcification (20%).
Sunburst pattern of vascularity (Internal Carotid & Ophthalmic artery supply).

content.explanation: Pseudo-FKS is much more common than true FKS. It is caused by sequential Non-Arteritic Ischemic Optic Neuropathy (NAION). The first eye has old atrophy, and the second eye presents with acute disc edema.

sections.title: Surgical Management Strategies
content: Step 1: Bifrontal Craniotomy (Standard for large tumors).
Step 2: Pterional Approach (Used for smaller, lateralized tumors).
Step 3: Endoscopic Endonasal Transcribriform Approach (Minimal access).
Step 4: Tumor Debulking and devascularization of the ethmoidal supply.
Step 5: Optic Canal Decompression (if vision is threatened).

rows: Total removal including dura and bone
Total removal + coagulation of dural attachment

sections.title: Red Flags & Urgent Considerations
content: Rapidly progressive vision loss (Emergency decompression needed)
CSF Rhinorrhea (Risk of meningitis)
New onset seizures (Frontal lobe irritation)
Mental status changes (Personality changes, apathy, or 'Frontal Lobe Syndrome')

sections.title: Surgical Complications
content: Anosmia: Permanent in almost all OGM surgical cases.
CSF Leak: High risk due to ethmoid bone manipulation.
Injury to ACoA: Anterior Communicating Artery complex is often draped over the tumor.
Venous Infarction: Damage to the Superior Sagittal Sinus.
Post-operative Diabetes Insipidus.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Anosmia is the 'silent' symptom—always test sense of smell in patients with unexplained optic atrophy.
The 'Dural Tail Sign' on MRI is characteristic but not pathognomonic for meningioma.
Frontal lobe syndrome (indifference, inappropriate behavior) can mimic depression or early dementia.
Meningiomas are hormone-sensitive; they may grow rapidly during pregnancy.
Stereotactic Radiosurgery (SRS) is a viable primary option for small tumors or as adjuvant for WHO Grade II/III.

content.explanation: F: Frontal Lobe tumor; O: Optic Atrophy (Ipsi); S: Swelling/Papilledema (Contra); T: Total Smell Loss (Anosmia).

sections.title: Pathophysiology Process
content: Tumor originates from arachnoid cells.
Expansile growth in subfrontal space.
Direct compression of Olfactory Nerve (CN I).
Encroachment on the Optic Canal/Intracranial Optic Nerve.
Increase in global ICP via mass effect or venous obstruction.
